result.title: 1. Introduction
result.summary: FPIF’s RFP seeks proposals for non-discretionary private-markets investment consulting and about three discretionary OCIO advisory mandates; forms are online, and respondents must monitor the website. Created by Illinois to manage investments for roughly 300 local firefighter pension funds, FPIF is governed by the Pension Code and a nine-member board; it began asset transitions in 2021 and managed $7.6 billion as of January 2023. Its 31% private-markets targets are 10% private equity, 7% private debt, 10% real estate, and 4% infrastructure. The consultant supports sourcing and recommendations across all asset classes, including specified buyout, growth, venture, direct-lending, core real-estate and infrastructure strategies. OCIO roles cover private equity (small/mid-market buyouts, growth, venture; global funds, secondaries and co-investments), real assets (non-core property, infrastructure and diversifying/opportunistic debt), and opportunistic strategies (niche, distressed and flexible equity and credit). The RFP details allocation splits, return goals, expertise and access expectations, possible staff veto/input, and a preference for separate accounts except potentially venture fund-of-funds. FPIF also seeks vendor diversity consistent with financial and fiduciary prudence.

result.title: 2. Proposal Content
key_items: 2.3. Minimum Qualifications Certification; 2.4. Description of Respondent’s Experience and Qualifications; 2.5. References; 2.6. Fee Proposal; 2.7 Additional Documentation and Data
2.4. Description of Respondent’s Experience and Qualifications
result.summary: RFP proposals must include every required component in separate sections, preferably in a zip file with a table of contents; noncompliance with the prescribed format may lead to rejection. The signed business-letter proposal cover must identify an authorized signatory and confirm compliance, truthfulness and completeness, offer validity for up to 360 days after the deadline, disclose relevant relationships or negotiations, acknowledge possible public disclosure, identify all proposal documents, certify no fraud, collusion, or improper remuneration, and accept Exhibit A certifications and terms. Complete Exhibit B in order, reproducing each question and number and answering fully without cross-references, and submit the Exhibit C minimum-qualification certification. Describe consulting experience, firm and relevant-class AUM/AUA and investment history, lead consultant/CIO experience, subcontracted services and oversight, and team roles. Provide three references, including a public defined-benefit plan client, with contact details; FPIF may contact them. Submit the all-inclusive Exhibit D fee proposal and Exhibit E documentation. Proposals may become public under Illinois FOIA; claimed confidential material must be identified in the transmission and on each page, with applicable exemptions and justifications, subject to FPIF’s determination.

result.title: 3. Timeline and Submission Requirements
result.summary: The procurement timeline is subject to FPIF’s discretion; updates will be posted on its website, which respondents must monitor. Dates: RFP issued February 13, 2023; questions due February 24 by noon Central; answers posted March 3; proposals due March 10 by noon Central; possible interviews in Q2/Q3 2023 and presentations in Q3/Q4 2023; anticipated Consultant selection May 26 and Discretionary Advisor selection August 25. Proposals must follow the RFP and be emailed as PDFs by the deadline to Mitchell Green (mgreen@ifpif.org) and investments@ifpif.org. Use the subject “Response to FPIF Private Markets Consulting and Advisory RFP – (Name of Respondent).” Late submissions may be excluded; only email submissions are accepted, with receipt confirmation. Proposals may be withdrawn by signed written notice received before the deadline, referencing the RFP title and respondent name. Modified proposals may be resubmitted by the deadline; other modification methods are not accepted.

result.title: 4. Procurement Rules and Procedure
key_items: 4.1. Procurement Rules; 4.2. Communications; Quiet Period; 4.3. Procurement Contact
result.summary: FPIF’s adopted procurement rules and applicable law govern the RFP, overseen by staff and advisors; it will publicly disclose the selected respondent, contract amount, fees, and selection factors. A quiet period runs from RFP issuance until selection or process closure: no procurement-related ex parte contact or attempts to influence evaluation are allowed, subject to ordinary-course, unrelated communications with existing service providers. Questions must go by email to Procurement Contact Mitchell Green by the stated deadline, using the required subject line; answers are posted anonymously in a consolidated Q&A, with no individual replies. Proposals are screened for completeness, accuracy, responsiveness, and minimum compliance, then assessed for best value using experience, capabilities, mandate fit, performance, risk, access, team and organizational factors, ethics, client references, pricing, ESG/DEI, location, and qualifying ownership status. FPIF may request clarifications or verification. Submissions become FPIF property and may be publicly disclosed; respondents bear their costs. FPIF reserves broad rights to reject, revise, cancel, waive, clarify, negotiate, request final offers, or disqualify, and may procure similar services elsewhere.

result.title: Exhibit A: Certifications and Terms Required by State Law
result.summary: Exhibit A lists 27 Illinois-law certifications and contractual commitments required of respondents entering an FPIF agreement; the terms will be incorporated into the agreement, and any inability to comply must be explained by item number in the proposal. They cover ethics, bribery and felony eligibility, state debt and use tax, environmental and lead-poisoning violations, conflicts and financial disclosures, political contributions, drug-free workplaces, bid-rigging, international boycotts, third-party fees, revolving-door restrictions, business registration, and reporting suspected anticompetitive conduct. Respondents must also meet nondiscrimination, affirmative-action, sexual-harassment-policy, discriminatory-club, and prevailing-wage requirements; retain and provide transition records for audit; notify FPIF about employee-solicitation plans; and recognize open-meetings and public-records laws. Further requirements address finance-entity status, annual minority/women/disability workforce and contracting disclosures, ownership disclosures, and disclosure and updating of subcontractors, marketers, and their expected compensation.

result.title: Exhibit B: Questionnaire
result.summary: Exhibit B requires a completed, ordered questionnaire covering respondent identity, contact details, business structure, ownership and control. It examines firm history, organization, locations, staffing, registrations, assets and clients, mandates, services, business lines, revenue, growth and diversity ownership. Respondents describe private-market products, advisory practices, client relationships, public-fund experience, investment approaches, sustainability policies, conflicts, legal or regulatory matters, audits, insurance, cybersecurity and continuity planning. The questionnaire covers team composition, diversity, proposed personnel, qualifications, responsibilities, client service, compensation, retention, turnover, leadership succession, compliance and legal support. Strategy questions address private equity, private debt, real assets and infrastructure, including investment philosophy, sourcing, due diligence, risk, allocations, GP relationships, market outlook, fees, manager access and performance. It requests fund, composite and mandate performance and capacity data. Operations questions address account availability and minimums, reporting timelines and systems, attribution, valuation and cash reconciliations, fee validation, compliance issues, competitive advantages and the firm’s fit as an FPIF partner.

nodes.title: Proposal Questionnaire: Company, Contacts, and Ownership
nodes.summary: Exhibit B requires the completed questionnaire to accompany the proposal, with each question listed before its answer and responses in questionnaire order. It collects company name, mailing address, state, ZIP code, city, phone, fax, website, and certified Federal Employer Identification Number, plus the contractor’s business entity type (including sole proprietorship, individual, corporation, nonprofit, LLC, governmental entity, or other). It requests contact person names, titles, phone numbers, fax numbers, and email addresses. Ownership information includes applicable entity types and, as required by the Pension Code, names and addresses of parent or controlling-interest entities, subsidiaries or entities controlled by the respondent, owners or distributive-income holders exceeding 7.5%, and executive officers.

nodes.title: Organization
nodes.summary: The RFP requests the contracting entity’s name and proposed mandates; firm founding, history, leadership and succession, institutional consulting/advisory experience, and senior-team tenure; headquarters and office addresses, staffing, departments, FPIF service locations, and Illinois presence; SEC registration and ADV Part II; and an organizational chart, anticipated changes, and growth plans. It seeks historical and current AUA/AUM by year, asset class, mandate type, client type, and client count, including private-market definitions, uncalled commitments, and explanations of ‘other.’ Respondents must describe private-market products and services, advisory approaches and differences between discretionary and non-discretionary work, client involvement, decision-making, care, communication, transparency, access to sought-after funds, and success with first- or second-fund managers. Requested client data includes five-year wins and losses and public-fund clients, with fund and mandate sizes and service dates or duration. The RFP also asks about business lines and revenue, parent-affiliate contributions, ownership and changes, employee ownership, and minority, women, or disability ownership, status, and certifications.

nodes.title: Firm Client Firm Private Market Count (#) AUA/AUM ($) AUA/AUM ($)
nodes.summary: The questionnaire requests information on the firm’s private-market products and services; advisory practices and differences between discretionary and non-discretionary mandates; access to oversubscribed funds and success backing first- or second-fund top-quartile managers. It seeks client-type AUA/AUM and private-market assets, explanations of “other,” client gains/losses and mandate details, and public-fund client histories. It covers growth plans, business lines and revenues, ownership and ownership changes, and diversity ownership, certification, workforce and investment-team demographics, plus diversity policies. It asks about business continuity and disaster recovery, physical and cybersecurity safeguards, breaches and third-party assessments, and insurance coverage. Further topics include opposition to FPIF or Illinois legislation, Illinois pension-fund advisory history, conflicts of interest, sustainability/ESG policies and UNPRI status, legal and regulatory proceedings, SEC audit findings and responses, and the current and previous auditor.

nodes.title: Team
nodes.summary: The section requests information on firm and investment-professional headcount, workforce diversity, and professionals supporting private equity, private debt, infrastructure, and real estate. It covers research-department structure; proposed mandate leads and account-team members, including biographies, experience, tenure, responsibilities, client loads, contact details, meeting attendance, team size, market coverage, and reporting charts. It asks how team stability is maintained, whether analysts specialize or generalize, how staff are evaluated and compensated, whether compensation is investment-linked, and how employee investments and other measures align interests. The firm must disclose overall and senior-staff turnover and investment-professional departures since 2018; leadership changes over ten years, planned departures, additions, succession plans, and expected retirements. It also requests client-service roles, biographies, and locations; any employee’s public-office candidacy or investment-fund trusteeship; the Chief Compliance Officer’s identity and biography; and whether legal services are in-house or external, including external counsel firms.

nodes.title: Strategy, Process, and Performance
nodes.summary: The RFP requests detailed information on firms proposing private equity or private debt solutions. For private equity, it covers experience, investment universe and strategy preferences; buyout, growth equity, venture, niche-market, co-investment and secondary capabilities; risk management, philosophy, sourcing, and investment, operational and legal due diligence; investment history, commitments, fund allocations, allocation policy, staffing, GP relationships and LPAC participation; proprietary funds, market outlook, competitive advantages and competitors; fee and carry mitigation; manager-return dispersion, top-quartile access, databases, screening deliverables, and performance. Requested evidence includes due-diligence checklists, pitchbooks, manager database counts by strategy, composite and fund-level returns, and public-market-equivalent performance tables. For private debt, it requests corresponding information on experience, universe, income/opportunistic/appreciation strategies, lending and distressed segments, niche sourcing, risk, proprietary funds, philosophy and due diligence, commitments and oversubscription allocation, sourcing, staffing, relationships, market outlook, advantages and competitors, fee mitigation, return dispersion, manager access, and performance.

nodes.title: June 30, 2022.
nodes.summary: The text includes a June 30, 2022 performance-table template with fund, investment, capital, valuation, return, and portfolio metrics, followed by an RFP asking firms proposing real-assets advisory or consulting solutions to address: experience and assets managed across core/non-core real estate and infrastructure; investment universe, biases, and preferred areas; core/non-core strategy views and allocation advice; risk management, philosophy, process, macro and public-market influences; fund sourcing and investment, operational, and legal due diligence; five-year commitments, fund counts, oversubscription, and capacity allocation; staffing, GP relationships, historical funds, and LPAC participation; market outlook and attractive sectors; strategy evaluation priorities; competitive advantages and competitors; fee and carried-interest mitigation; access to top-performing managers; and flagship-fund or representative-composite performance.

nodes.title: June 30, 2022.
nodes.summary: Dated June 30, 2022, this FPIF RFP Exhibit B1 requests performance data, where available, for four composites: Core and Non-Core Real Estate, and Core and Non-Core Infrastructure. A table is to be completed for each composite, listing funds and totals, investment vintage, fund size, committed and invested capital, number of investments, realized proceeds, unrealized and total value, gross and net MOIC and IRR, DPI, RVPI, and TVPI. A second table requests each strategy’s inception date, committed capital, number of funds, and 1-, 3-, 5-, 10-year and since-inception IRRs. Questions ask whether the firm has asset-class capacity constraints or policies limiting AUM in proposed mandates; the sizes and inception dates of its five largest substantially similar consulting/advisory mandates from unique investors as of December 31, 2022; and its largest, smallest, average, and median client sizes.

nodes.title: Operations
nodes.summary: The operations section asks whether the strategies are available through separately managed accounts and whether minimum account sizes apply; expected turnaround for quarterly and annual performance reports; any significant compliance or ethics violations and their handling and resolution; the firm’s competitive advantages and case for selection; and client-facing software for reporting, sourcing, and evaluating strategies. It requests a sample quarterly report and details on private-markets attribution capabilities, reporting by asset class and manager, and online access. It also asks about GP financial reporting requirements and reconciliation procedures for investment valuations, commitments, paid-in and invested capital, distributions, expenses, management fees, and cash, including reconciliation with client custodians. Finally, it asks whether fee monitoring or validation is offered and how the firm is uniquely positioned to partner with FPIF.

result.title: Exhibit C: Minimum Qualifications Certification
result.summary: Exhibit C is a minimum-qualifications certification form to be completed, signed, and included with the proposal. The company certifies that it is a registered investment adviser or identifies its exemption; will act as an Illinois Pension Code fiduciary if retained; holds all required authorizations, permits, licenses, and certifications; assigns a senior account professional with at least 10 years’ industry experience; has at least $500 million in assets under management and five years of performance history in the proposed asset classes; has experience managing investments for tax-exempt or governmental defined-benefit plans; and has operated as an investment management organization for at least 10 years. Experience, assets, and operating-history thresholds are measured as of December 31, 2022. The form includes fields for the company, authorized signer’s name and title, signature, and date. Respondents that do not meet every minimum qualification should not submit a proposal to FPIF.

Please provide a fee proposal for the proposed mandate(s). Consultants should propose a flat annual fee structure for private markets consulting. Consultants that offer both general consulting and private market consulting should also submit a joint fee proposal for both services. Discretionary Advisors should propose a flat fee or asset-based management fee. Incentive compensation will be considered.

result.title: Exhibit E: Additional Documentation and Data
result.summary: Exhibit E requires respondents to attach all documents requested in Exhibit B and provide: ADV Part II; allocation policy; biographies of consultants, account leads, proposed senior personnel, and the chief compliance officer; investment, operational, and legal due diligence checklists; code of ethics or professional conduct; corporate social responsibility, diversity, sustainability, and/or ESG policies; disaster recovery and business continuity plans; a pitchbook or standard marketing presentation for proposed strategies; proof of E&O, professional liability, fiduciary, and other insurance coverage; a sample quarterly investment performance report; an SEC review findings letter; and, if applicable, state or local minority certification/registration and a GIPS verification letter. The material is part of the FPIF Request for Proposals.
